baseline_models.mechanism: A group defined by covering or rejecting truth is nevertheless held in an exposed, sustained gaze on the addressee; concealment and visual fixation form a contradiction.

activation_trace.role: Covering or rejecting truth supplies the concealing stance that the visible posture exposes.
Being on the facing side fixes the concealed group's orientation relative to the addressee.
Fixing and sustaining the gaze turns bodily attention into involuntary disclosure.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers are merely assembled before the addressee.
changed_reading.after: The question exposes denial as a posture that cannot stop looking toward the one it rejects.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence from كَفَرُوا through قِبَلَكَ to مُهْطِعِينَ joins identity, direction, and movement.
baseline_models.mechanism: Repudiation and forward arrival pull in opposite directions: those who disavow are bodily rushing into encounter with what they disavow.

activation_trace.role: Disavowal supplies the relational withdrawal that their subsequent movement reverses.
One thing facing another gives the encounter a direct opposing axis.
Hurrying forward converts static opposition into a paradoxical approach.

changed_reading.before: They hurry in the addressee's direction.
changed_reading.after: Their bodies reverse their declared relation: repudiators rush into the encounter from which repudiation withdraws.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The posture word مُهْطِعِينَ and the addressee-facing construction remain explicit even under a form-distant branch of ك ف ر.
baseline_models.mechanism: Lowered or projected heads, compliance, and a bowed branch of the denial root allow the body to leak a submission that the stated identity withholds.

activation_trace.role: Bowed submission supplies an exploratory bodily counter-image inside the root naming the deniers.
A body part turned forward gives the possible submission a concrete directional posture.
Lowering or projecting the neck and head supplies the visible carriage of the body.
Humility and compliance make that carriage read as subjection rather than mere speed.

changed_reading.before: The crowd consists of urgent spectators.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, their addressee-facing necks already enact the subjection their denial refuses to name.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening event is painful, falls into fixed occurrence, and cannot be pushed aside; they see it as distant while the counter-seeing places it temporally near. The deniers' fixed gaze and forward haste can therefore register bodily knowledge of a nearness their denial misreads.

activation_trace.role: Covering or rejecting truth supplies the cognitive resistance whose bodily contradiction is exposed.
A sustained gaze gives the body a perceptual signal distinct from the stated estimate of distance.
Hurrying forward makes the supposedly distant event exert present kinetic urgency.
Pain and punishment identify what the crowd has reason to hold cognitively at a distance.
Falling and becoming fixed supplies the event's irreversible downward pressure.
Pushing away an unwanted thing supplies the failed resistance explicitly denied in the context.
Seeing by eye or insight marks their distance judgment as a mode of perception.
The repeated seeing branch supplies the opposed vantage from which the same event is near.
Distance from nearness gives their explicit estimate its separating force.
Temporal approach and impending completion relocate the event into the body's urgent present.

structural_cues: 70:6 and 70:7 place opposed evaluations of distance in consecutive clauses with the same seeing construction.
The opening sequence moves from requested punishment to fixed occurrence and the absence of any repeller.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: an unrepellable event, opposed distance judgments, and a fixed or hurrying focus posture. Reader arrow: the body registers the nearness that denial misperceives. Live alternative: the crowd's gaze and speed may concern only the addressee, not the event.

changed_reading.before: Their stare and haste show intense attention to the addressee.
changed_reading.after: Their bodies betray the present pressure of what they call distant: fixed gaze and haste become somatic evidence against their own estimate.

context_deltas.mechanism: The fire calls one who turned the back, turned away, gathered, and enclosed. Against that sequence, the focus crowd is directionally split: bodies hurry forward while allegiance retreats and possessions close inward.

activation_trace.role: Disavowal supplies relational withdrawal beneath the crowd's visible advance.
Direct facing supplies the forward axis against which turning away can be measured.
Hurrying forward intensifies the contradiction between bodily approach and ethical retreat.
Calling and drawing by speech supplies a counter-summons beneath the apparent approach to the addressee.
Showing the back and withdrawing supplies the first ethical vector opposite the focus movement.
Turning away and retreating doubles the backward vector as a chosen relation.
Joining dispersed things into a collection supplies the acquisitive inward movement.
Enclosing something in a vessel closes the gathered material against outward circulation.

structural_cues: The feminine call in 70:17 continues the fire scene immediately before it.
70:18 pairs collecting with enclosing in a two-verb sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: a caller, paired turning-away verbs, and paired collecting-enclosing verbs. Reader arrow: these vectors diagnose the focus crowd's forward motion as bodily approach without relational approach. Live alternative: their present advance could be hostile crowd behavior unrelated to the earlier directional sequence.

changed_reading.before: The deniers are simply moving toward the addressee.
changed_reading.after: They are split-direction people: feet and faces advance, allegiance turns its back, and accumulated goods move into closure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context contrasts withholding beneficial good with a maintained, owner-specific right in wealth for the asker and deprived. Activated by the favor-covering branch of ك ف ر and a receiving branch of ق ب ل, the rush becomes a one-way claim to receive without releasing what is due.

activation_trace.role: Covering over a favor supplies the failure to acknowledge and circulate received good.
Receiving with acceptance supplies the crowd's one-way orientation toward acquisition.
Hurrying forward turns the receptive orientation into appetite rather than passive location.
Inclination toward beneficial good supplies the desirable resource around which conduct is tested.
Withholding the hand from giving supplies the blocked outward flow.
Acquiring and multiplying wealth supplies the stored medium in which an outward claim exists.
A specific right possessed by its owner makes distribution an obligation rather than optional generosity.
Asking and requesting identifies one claimant toward whom wealth should move.
Deprivation and missing the desired thing identifies the claimant who lacks access even without asking.

structural_cues: 70:21 states withholding when good touches, while 70:24-25 gives the counter-pattern of a known right for two recipients.
The focus question follows the completed list of people whose repeated practices keep goods, testimony, trust, and prayer in circulation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: beneficial good, withholding, wealth, a fixed right, an asker, and a deprived person. Reader arrow: the crowd's receiving orientation is read as acquisitive asymmetry. Live alternative: their haste may be hostile or curious rather than a claim to benefit.

changed_reading.before: A hostile or curious crowd presses toward the addressee.
changed_reading.after: The crowd embodies one-way reception: those who cover favor hurry to receive while the surrounding ethical sequence requires wealth to move toward others.

context_deltas.mechanism: Honored people are already inside a tree-covered garden, while each member of the crowd covets admission to that same sheltered good state. The shared covering image of ك ف ر and ج ن ن turns the addressee-facing rush into pressure at a threshold: coverers of truth seek entry into a covering that protects and honors.

activation_trace.role: Covering and concealment supplies one side of the cross-root contrast between denial and desired shelter.
Standing on the facing side places the addressee at the crowd's inferred threshold.
Hurrying forward turns threshold orientation into pressure for access.
A garden covered by trees supplies the protected enclosure occupied by the honored group.
Praiseworthy honor supplies the status attached to being inside that enclosure.
The heart's coveting and hope explicitly supplies the motive for the crowd's approach.
Passing into an interior makes access, rather than mere proximity, the desired transition.
The repeated tree-covered garden identifies the enclosure each crowd member wants to enter.
Good condition and blessing supply the attractive interior state attached to the garden.

structural_cues: 70:35 places the honored inside gardens; 70:36-38 moves directly from the crowd before the addressee to each member's wish to be admitted.
The interrogative in 70:38 distributes the desire across every individual in the surrounding crowd.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: honored garden occupants, a rushing crowd, and each crowd member coveting garden entry. Reader arrow: the addressee-facing position is treated as threshold pressure, and the two covering branches are put in contrast. Live alternative: 70:38 may expose an expectation without supplying the motive for the movement in 70:36.

changed_reading.before: The crowd rushes toward the addressee for an unspecified reason.
changed_reading.after: They press a threshold, trying to convert proximity into admission: those who cover truth covet the covered garden of honor.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate continuation distributes the crowd on the right and left. The focus-facing relation therefore becomes a radial formation: separate bands face a center from both flanks, creating social pressure rather than a single line of approach.

activation_trace.role: A mutually facing group supplies the relational geometry organized around the addressee.
Sustained gaze makes each flank maintain orientation toward the same center.
Forward hurry adds pressure from the distributed sides toward that center.
The right hand and rightward side supplies one explicit flank of the formation.
The leftward side supplies the opposed flank completing the spatial distribution.
Surrounding from the sides turns the two directions into an enveloping pressure field.

structural_cues: 70:37 is a direct syntactic continuation of مُهْطِعِينَ and supplies the paired prepositional phrases from the right and from the left.
The continuation labels the people عِزِينَ; that word is used here only as a grouping cue, without assigning it a branch image.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: sustained forward orientation plus explicit right and left positions. Reader arrow: the two flanks are modeled as a center-facing pressure field. Live alternative: the phrases may only locate scattered groups without implying encirclement or pressure.

changed_reading.before: Individuals hurry toward the addressee along one forward path.
changed_reading.after: Fractured bands converge from both flanks, making the addressee the organizing center of a surrounding formation.

context_deltas.mechanism: What looks in the focus like purposeful straight-line haste is later described as plunging into and stirring a medium, acting without a sound aim, and continuing only until a face-to-face convergence at an appointed time. The crowd's direction is thus apparent; its actual trajectory is a bounded eddy ending in forced meeting.

activation_trace.role: Direct facing supplies the apparent purposeful line that the later sequence reclassifies.
Hurrying forward supplies the visible momentum carried into the later bounded interval.
Entering into water supplies the medium-like motion that replaces a clean directed path.
Action without a sound intended end deprives the crowd's speed of genuine purpose.
Two things arriving face-to-face supplies the terminal convergence of the trajectory.
An appointment fixed by time or place supplies the boundary at which aimless motion ends.

structural_cues: The imperative in 70:42 leaves them to two coordinated activities only until a specified meeting.
The temporal حَتَّىٰ construction makes their apparently free movement terminate at a fixed horizon.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: hurrying, plunging, aimless play, meeting, and appointment. Reader arrow: the present crowd motion is read as an eddy within the later bounded trajectory. Live alternative: 70:42 may describe subsequent conduct without retrospectively classifying the movement in 70:36.

changed_reading.before: Their speed indicates a clear intention toward the addressee.
changed_reading.after: Their haste only looks directed; it belongs to an aimless current whose true endpoint is the appointment they must meet.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing scene reproduces the focus ayah's directional body in expanded form: emergence from graves, speed toward an erected marker, lowered gaze, overtaking pressure, broken humiliation, and compliant haste. The present addressee-facing posture becomes an anticipatory bodily rhyme with a future compelled procession.

activation_trace.role: Direct facing supplies the directional axis repeated by movement toward the later marker.
Fixing and sustaining the gaze supplies the visual posture later inverted into lowered eyes.
Lowering or projecting the neck and head supplies the bridge to the closing scene's bowed visual carriage.
Hurrying forward supplies the repeated speed signature.
Humility and compliance supplies the agency shift from eager-looking movement to compelled procession.
Passing out of an interior supplies the mass emergence that begins the later procession.
The grave supplies the enclosing origin from which the repeated crowd motion erupts.
Speed as the opposite of slowness directly reinforces the haste branch of مُهْطِعِينَ.
An erected, conspicuous marker supplies the later directional target corresponding to the focus-facing axis.
Lowering and submission gives the later eyes the subdued posture latent in the focus neck and head.
Overtaking and overpowering supplies the external pressure that changes haste into compulsion.
Brokenness under domination supplies the humiliating outcome of the bodily rhyme.
Compliant haste fuses the closing scene's speed and submission into one motion.

structural_cues: 70:43 explicitly compares their motion to movement toward a نصب and 70:44 immediately supplies altered gaze and humiliation.
The occurrence of و ف ض at 70:43 word 9 has no branch inventory; it supports the hurrying parallel only as an uncited structural cue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the focus posture and a later sequence of grave-exit, speed, directed motion, lowered gaze, pressure, and humiliation. Reader arrow: the present posture is an anticipatory bodily rhyme with the future procession. Live alternative: the two passages may share only generic crowd kinetics without a deliberate anticipatory relation.

changed_reading.before: The focus depicts a present crowd staring and hurrying toward the addressee.
changed_reading.after: Their present bodies rehearse their future procession: the same direction, gaze, neck, speed, and compliance return under overt compulsion and humiliation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because قِبَلَكَ is locative and does not itself state a ritual qibla or worship. It remains anchored in the prayer-facing and mutually facing branches of ق ب ل, the compliant posture of ه ط ع, and the surrounding repeated-prayer frame. Downstream prose must present it only as geometric analogy, never as a claim that the crowd worships the addressee.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قِبَلَكَ at word 4 organizes a plural, compliant-looking crowd toward one center.

activation_trace.role: Rejection of truth prevents the geometric analogy from being mistaken for genuine devotion.
Prayer-facing direction supplies the qibla-like geometry of orientation toward one center.
A mutually facing group turns the plural crowd into a congregation-like arrangement.
Humility and compliance supplies the outward posture that makes the analogy visually possible.
Specified worship supplies the genuine practice against which the crowd's geometry looks counterfeit.
Stillness and continuity supplies the durable quality absent from a momentary rush.
Persistent maintenance supplies the second marker of genuine prayer orientation missing from crowd posture.

changed_reading.before: The crowd happens to face the addressee.
changed_reading.after: As a contained analogy, it forms a counterfeit congregation: direction and compliant posture without the durable practice that makes orientation truthful.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because the farmer's covering of seed is not the ordinary gloss of كَفَرُوا here. It remains packet-anchored through that focus branch and the later sequence of garden vegetation, grave, exit, and speed. Downstream prose must label it a material analogy, not replace the lexical sense of disbelief or assert a botanical identity.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: كَفَرُوا at word 3 carries a seed-covering branch, while مُهْطِعِينَ at word 5 supplies directed haste.

activation_trace.role: Covering seed with earth supplies the remote agricultural image underlying the material analogy.
Hurrying forward gives the imagined emergence its rapid directed motion.
Intertwining and thrusting vegetation supplies the growing enclosure at the far side of the analogy.
Passing from inside to outside supplies emergence from prior enclosure.
The grave supplies the earth enclosure that makes the buried-seed comparison materially legible.
Speed opposite slowness turns emergence into a sudden mass procession.

changed_reading.before: The focus presents a crowd of deniers in rapid approach.
changed_reading.after: As a material analogy only, seed-coverers become an earth-covered mass whose later emergence is rapid and directed toward the cultivated enclosure they covet.

strongest_changes: The fixed gaze and haste can be the body's admission that the supposedly distant, unrepellable event is already near.
The crowd presses a garden threshold: those who cover truth covet entry into the covered enclosure of honor.
Right and left convert simple approach into a center-facing formation of separate bands.
The closing grave-rush repeats and transforms the focus posture into compelled speed, lowered gaze, and humiliation.
summary.what_was_special: Repeated bodily geometry did the main work: covering versus covered garden, facing versus turning away, fixed gaze versus mistaken distance, and present haste versus the later grave procession produced several coexisting readings without dissolving the focus words into general themes.
remaining_uncertainties: مُهْطِعِينَ can weight sustained gaze, neck carriage, speed, or compliance differently; the packet keeps all four live.
The 70:43-44 posture may be a deliberate anticipatory echo of 70:36 or only a recurrence of crowd kinetics.
The threshold and counterfeit-congregation readings depend on branch activation beyond a strictly locative reading of قِبَلَكَ.
